subject: maths
title: Column Addition and Subtraction
seo_title: Year 3 Column Addition and Subtraction Worksheets: 3-Digit Numbers, Exchanging and Checking
standard_text: Add and subtract numbers with up to three digits, using formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction; estimate the answer to a calculation and use inverse operations to check answers; solve problems, including missing number problems, using number facts, place value, and more complex addition and subtraction.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on column addition and subtraction with 3-digit numbers, following the National Curriculum: exchanging, subtracting across a zero, estimating, checking with the inverse, missing numbers and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Line up the ones. Start on the right. Exchange when you need to.
key_sub: Adding: if a column makes 10 or more, exchange 1 into the next column. Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, exchange 1 from the next column. Check with the inverse or an estimate.
body_html:
The idea: line up the columns

Write the numbers in columns. Put ones under ones, tens under tens and hundreds under hundreds. Always start with the ones on the right.

If a column adds up to 10 or more, write the ones digit. Then exchange 10 for 1 in the next column. Write the exchanged 1 small, under the answer line.

Two exchanges

What is 367 + 258?

Ones: 7 + 8 = 15. Write 5 and exchange 1 ten. Tens: 6 + 5 + 1 = 12. Write 2 and exchange 1 hundred. Hundreds: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

Answer: 625

Column subtraction with exchanging

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, exchange. Take 1 from the next column and make 10 more in this column. Cross out the old digit and write the new one above it.

Exchanging across a zero

If the tens digit is 0, there are no tens to take. First exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens. Then exchange 1 ten for 10 ones. The 0 becomes 9.

Check your answer

Use the inverse. Addition and subtraction undo each other. To check 452 − 178 = 274, add: 274 + 178 = 452. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

Estimate. Round each number and do an easier sum. 452 − 178 is about 450 − 180 = 270. An answer of 274 is sensible. An answer of 326 is not.

Missing numbers and word problems

For a missing number, use the inverse. For ☐ + 145 = 403, work out 403 − 145 = 258. In a word problem, ask: am I putting together (add) or taking away and finding the difference (subtract)?

Two steps

A school trip costs £800. The cake sale raised £356 and the fair raised £287. How much more is needed?

Step 1, money raised: £356 + £287 = £643. Step 2, money still needed: £800 − £643 = £157.

Answer: £157

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the exchanged 1 (367 + 258 = 515)Write the exchanged 1 under the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the bigger one (452 − 178 = 326)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Exchange when the top is smaller
Not exchanging across a zero (402 − 158 = 254)Exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens first. The 0 becomes 9
Lining up the numbers on the left (345 + 23 = 575)Line up the ones on the right: 345 + 23 = 368

faq.q: Do Year 3 children learn column addition and subtraction?
faq.a: Yes. The National Curriculum says Year 3 pupils should add and subtract numbers with up to three digits using the formal written methods of column addition and subtraction.

faq.q: What does “exchange” mean in column subtraction?
faq.a: Exchanging means swapping 1 from the next column for 10 in this column, for example 1 ten for 10 ones. It is what older books call borrowing or carrying.

faq.q: How do you subtract across a zero, like 402 − 158?
faq.a: Exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens, then 1 ten for 10 ones. 402 becomes 3 hundreds, 9 tens and 12 ones, and the answer is 244.

faq.q: How can my child check an addition or subtraction answer?
faq.a: Use the inverse: for 452 − 178 = 274, check that 274 + 178 = 452. A quick estimate, such as 450 − 180 = 270, also shows whether the answer is sensible.

sets.title: Estimate and check with the inverse

items.q: Which calculation checks 523 − 178 = 345?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. Add the answer to the number you took away: 345 + 178 = 523. That is the number you started with, so the answer is right.

items.q: Which calculation checks 604 − 257 = 347?

items.q: Which calculation checks 812 − 369 = 443?

items.q: Which calculation checks 368 + 245 = 613?
items.e: Subtraction is the inverse of addition. Take one of the numbers away from the answer: 613 − 245 = 368. You get the other number, so the answer is right.

items.q: Which calculation checks 457 + 286 = 743?
items.e: Subtraction is the inverse of addition. Take one of the numbers away from the answer: 743 − 286 = 457. You get the other number, so the answer is right.
